title: Dated Poseidon transform and memory experiments: reviewed scientific extracts
status: SOURCE-REPORTED counts and closures; not independently replayed
scope: Four complete, specifically selected scientific ledger entries covering three engineering topics. The surrounding mixed coordination ledger is not admitted as publication text.

provenance.selection_rule: Preserve numerical result, scope, credited method and missing evidence. Omit commands, queue/filing instructions and unrelated coordination. These are new paraphrases, not copied external text.

records.status: Reported negative count for the specified r9/r13/r15 schedules
records.finding: The tested three-array C/D schedule increased the time exponent by about 0.36 to 0.65 bits, while the realized memory improvement was only about 0.03 to 0.04 bits because stage D and Newton workspace still constrained the peak. The ledger records every tested case as worse or short of its intended improvement threshold.
records.correction: The same entry rejects the earlier r15 score 90.96140 because its PD_KMAXJ=34 setting exceeded the relevant 2-adicity limit. It records 90.98045 at PD_KMAXJ=31 as the valid comparison.
records.evidence_boundary: The cited scratchpad/api11 directory was not found at the workspace root or under research during this bounded review. This is a preserved report, not a newly verified count or an all-algorithm memory lower bound.

records.status: Reported lower-bound argument for a selected implementation family
records.finding: The r17 entry identifies three n1-sized arrays R,W,g as the stage-C floor for its non-in-place squaring layout. The evaluated in-place alternative is reported to require at least twice the stage-C work, causing about +0.683 time bits against a 0.62-bit saving budget and leaving the score at least about 100.04.
records.evidence_boundary: The underlying derivation and exact implementation of the cited Giorgi–Grenet–Roche-style alternative were not located or replayed in this bounded review. The report leaves a cheaper in-place squaring open. It is not a universal lower bound for every representation, recomputation strategy or future implementation.

records.status: Reported cross-row gain and loss; no new replay
records.finding: The B2 variant places stage-B kappa inverse-transform work on stage-C column passes and uses a natural-order point loop. The ledger reports about a 0.0083-bit improvement at r14 but a loss at small kappa, including r9.
records.attribution: The ledger identifies mpjunior92 entries 4a13fe68, 3a4f2047 and 755611f3, and akki-rock05's lower-row port 67fe23d7.
records.evidence_boundary: This short entry does not provide a complete transform identity, operation numerator or allocator trace. The separate r9 Graeffe improvement on the same source line is not attributed to B2. No predecessor proof text is reproduced.

records.status: Reported negative recount, not independently executed
records.finding: For the proposed stage-C coset group of size 3*2^32, the ledger replaces an estimated 3.3% saving with a recounted 5.4% increase in stage C and 4.2% more memory. Its reported overall score is 72.29947 versus 72.18682. The source attributes the mismatch to an underpriced radix-3 pass of roughly 8.5 operations per point.
records.control: Even assigning the fused radix-3 work zero cost gives a reported score of 72.25275, still worse than the baseline. The tested VSHIFT=2 alternative lowers stage-C work but loses after memory is scored.
records.evidence_boundary: No exact numerator, complete parameter snapshot or replay script is attached to this ledger entry. These numerical comparisons are retained as source-reported results, not recertified costs or a rejection of all radix-3 algorithms.

publication_rights: Scientific paraphrase of the project's own ledger; no ordinary chat, external paper payload or predecessor proof copied. The original mixed ledger should not be exported through this note.
review_limitations: Only the four selected entries were reviewed for this note, not the entire ledger.
No research computation was run. Missing local scratchpad paths are not proof the artifacts do not exist on another system.
The exact dated counts are valuable negative evidence, but replay requires recovering the original parameter and program snapshots.
